key_concepts: Solubility is the property of a substance to dissolve in a given solvent.
Solutes can be solid, liquid, or gas.
Water is called the universal solvent.
For solid and liquid solutes, increasing temperature increases the rate of solubility.
For gaseous solutes, lower temperature increases solubility over higher temperature.
Stirring or agitation increases the rate at which a solute dissolves.
The nature of the solute and solvent affects solubility.
Polar solvents like water dissolve polar solutes but not nonpolar solutes.
Pressure mainly affects the solubility of gases.
Increasing pressure on a gas increases its solubility.
Smaller particle size increases the rate of solubility because of greater surface area.
The amount of solvent affects solubility.
